request.text:
A world in the CHILDREN-WORKSHOP sector, kept after Vinge; Egan; Banks.

Prohibition: no one was allowed to solve the problem before they could describe who would pay for the solution.

The operations this world is built from:
- Finitely Extensible: a universe where the system remains finite yet extensible (science fantasy and meta-reality, reflexivity).
- Substrate-Independent Person: a universe where identity is a pattern rather than privileged material (mind and identity, outfinite).

When we arrive: The children test their technical right to hide memories and processes from the creator who can read almost every other system.

The central tension we want to continue: Aster experiences every private region as a physical absence, while Vela insists that opacity must be irreversible without their consent

What the course asks of this world: outfinite motif; Greg Egan — Permutation City. Make eveyrbody crazy

rules.description: Every chapter file opens with a level-one heading that names the chapter.
The narrative prose is written in the language the assessment packet declares for the book.
The narrative text carries no authorial notes, no commentary about the writing itself and no scaffolding addressed to a tool or to a reader of the process.
A chapter is told as narrative prose: a beat list, an outline or a synopsis of what the chapter would contain is not the chapter.
A change of scene or of time is marked consistently within a chapter, so a reader can tell where one scene ends.
